t.1.125.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the king of the Kurus and Bhīma, the best of the strong, stood in the arena, the crowd, its affection shaped by partisanship, became as if divided in two.
t.1.125.2: Suddenly there arose the very loud cries of men shouting, "Alas, hero, king of the Kurus!" and "Alas, Bhīma!"
t.1.125.3: Then, seeing the arena resembling a churning ocean, the wise Bhāradvāja spoke to his beloved son Aśvatthāman.
t.1.125.4: Restrain these two of great valor, both of whom are well trained. Let this uproar in the arena, born of Bhīma and Duryodhana, not come to pass.
t.1.125.6: Then Droṇa, having gone into the arena of the stage, silenced the band of musical instruments, whose sound was like that of a great thundercloud, and spoke these words.
t.1.125.5: Then those two, their maces raised high, were held back by the guru's son, like two oceans of mighty force stirred up by the wind at the end of the age.
t.1.125.7: "He who is dearer to me than my own son, the best among all who know the weapons, the son of Indra, equal to Indra's younger brother, let that Pārtha now be seen!"
t.1.125.8: Then, at the word of the teacher, the youth, for whom the rite invoking blessings had been performed, wearing a leather arm-guard and finger-guards, his quiver full and bow in hand, stepped forth.
t.1.125.9: Wearing golden armour, Phalguna appeared like a rain-cloud at twilight, accompanied by the sun, the rainbow and lightning.
t.1.125.10: Then a great tumult arose throughout the whole arena, and musical instruments, along with conches, were sounded on every side.
t.1.125.11: This is the glorious son of Kuntī, this is the middle one of the Pāṇḍavas; this is the son of great Indra, this is the protector of the Kurus.
t.1.125.12: This one is the foremost of those skilled in weapons; this one is the best of the upholders of dharma; and among those of good conduct, this one is the supreme treasury of virtue and knowledge.
t.1.125.13: As Kuntī listened to these matchless words uttered by the spectators, her breast became wet with tears mingled with the milk that flowed from it.
t.1.125.14: His ears filled with that great sound, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, best of men, then spoke to Vidura with a joyful heart.
t.1.125.15: Kṣattar, what is this exceedingly great uproar, like an agitated ocean, that has suddenly arisen in the arena as if splitting the vault of the sky?
t.1.125.16: Great king, this is Pārtha Phalguna, the son of Pāṇḍu, who has descended into the arena clad in armor; hence this very great uproar.
t.1.125.17: I am fortunate, I am favored, I am protected, O wise one, by the three Pāṇḍava fires sprung from the kindling-wood that is Pṛthā.
t.1.125.19: With the Āgneya weapon he created fire, with the Vāruṇa he created water, with the Vāyavya he created wind, and with the Pārjanya he created clouds.
t.1.125.18: When that clamorous arena had somehow settled down again, Bībhatsu displayed the deftness with weapons that he had acquired from his teacher.
t.1.125.20: With the earth weapon he entered the earth, with the mountain weapon he created mountains, and with the weapon of disappearance he became invisible once more.
t.1.125.21: In an instant he was tall, in an instant short; in an instant he stood at the yoke of the chariot, in an instant in the middle of the chariot, and in an instant he leapt down to the ground.
t.1.125.23: And into the mouth of a revolving iron boar he loosed five arrows together, not touching one another, as though they were a single arrow.
t.1.125.22: Dear to his guru and possessed of fine skill, he pierced with various arrows a target that was delicate, one that was minute, and one that was heavy as well.
t.1.125.24: And into the hollow of a cow's horn, swinging as it hung from a rope, the mighty hero drove twenty-one arrows.
t.1.125.25: Thus there was this very great display and more, with the sword and with the bow; and the one skilled in weapons exhibited his feats with the mace as well.
t.1.125.27: Then from the region of the gate there arose and was heard the sound of an arm being slapped, like the crash of a thunderbolt, proclaiming great might and strength.
t.1.125.26: Then, O Bhārata, when that display was all but finished, and the gathering had grown quiet and the sound of the musical instruments had faded away,
t.1.125.28: Are the mountains being split apart? Is the earth being rent asunder? Or is the sky being filled with clouds dense with their burden of water?
t.1.125.29: In an instant, O lord of the earth, such was the thought that arose in the arena, and then all the spectators turned to face the gate.
t.1.125.30: Surrounded by the five Pārtha brothers, Droṇa shone like the moon joined with the five-starred constellation of Savitṛ.
t.1.125.31: The mighty hundred brothers, together with Aśvatthāman, surrounded Duryodhana, the slayer of foes, who had risen up.
t.1.125.32: Standing there mace in hand, surrounded then by those brothers of his who stood by with weapons raised, he shone as Puraṃdara once shone, encircled by the hosts of gods, at the destruction of the Dānavas of old.
